To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

myostatin is expressed at higher levels than MyoD during the formation of muscle fibers in normal and double-muscling cattle, and that myostatin expression is greater in double than normal-muscling cattle.

myostatin expression is greater in the double-muscled condition and peaks during the onset of secondary muscle fiber formation, and MyoD and myogenin mRNA are elevated throughout the formation of secondary muscle fibers.
myostatin mRNA and MyoD expression are greater in DM fetuses than NM fetuses, suggesting that myostatin is a negative regulator of MyoD expression and muscle development in cattle.

the molecular basis of the excessive muscling in double muscled cattle.
the molecular regulation of muscle growth in the bovine fetus, which has direct relevance to the production of beef cattle and may provide insight for human muscle disorders.
the temporal and quantitative relationship between myostatin and the myogenic regulatory factors in cattle.
